structure.layout: npm workspaces monorepo (packages/*, apps/*), ESM, Node >=22.18, package name frisson
structure.language: TypeScript ~5.8.3; the API runs .ts directly via node

packages.apps/web: @frisson/web. Vue 3, Vue Router, Pinia SPA on Vite 6. Typecheck with vue-tsc. Sources in apps/web/src (components, views, stores, composables, utils, forms, router, App).
packages.apps/api: @frisson/api. Fastify 5 with zod type provider. SQLite via better-sqlite3 and drizzle-orm. Tests in apps/api/test.
packages.packages/shared: @frisson/shared. Zod schemas and sorting. Typecheck only.

structure.buildSystem: Root scripts: dev, build, typecheck, test, lint (eslint .), format, format:check. Playwright ^1.65 is a root dev dependency.

tests.notes: Run from the repo root. Single file: npm test -w apps/web -- src/views/CrateView.test.ts. Typecheck: npm run typecheck. Lint: npm run lint.
tests.browser: No Playwright config or e2e script. .shipyard/checks/browser.mjs is a Playwright script printing PASS/FAIL per criterion. README documents DATA_DIR temp + SEED_DEMO_DATA=false for browser checks.

conventions.formatting: Prettier: no semis, single quotes, width 100, trailing commas all. Editorconfig: lf, 2 spaces.
conventions.lint: ESLint 9 flat config with eslint-plugin-vue flat/essential and @vue/eslint-config-typescript. Prettier owns style.
conventions.ci: .github/workflows/ci.yml: npm ci, format:check, lint, typecheck, test, build, plus docker smoke test
conventions.webStructure: src/api, stores (Pinia), views (*View.vue), components by feature (album/, crate/, forms/, profile/), composables (useXxx.ts), utils (plain functions)
conventions.naming: Vue files PascalCase; composables useXxx.ts; tests *.test.ts next to source
conventions.git: Conventional Commits with scope, e.g. fix(web): ...; ADRs for significant decisions

documentation.gaps: No CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING or CHANGELOG. docs/SPEC.md repo tree is an early plan and differs from the actual files.

relevant.summary: The per-crate add controls already check ownership. The remaining leak is the global toolbar, LibraryToolbar.vue. It shows 'Edit crates' and '+ Add a record' to any signed-in user, even on another user's crate. The same toolbar renders on /shelf and /list. The 'New crate' form lives only on /crates (CratesView) and is shown to every signed-in user on purpose.

current_user_and_permission.note: Pinia session store. It holds user (PublicUser|null) and the computeds signedIn and isAdmin.
canEditCrate(user, crate) returns false if there is no user or crate, true for admins, otherwise true only when crate.ownerId === user.id. The comment says it only decides which controls to show.
Holds library.crates, crateById, selectedCrate and crateShelves. Each crate carries ownerId, ownerUsername and ownerDisplayName (see CrateView.vue:127). I did not open this file.

render_sites.note: Likely locus of the bug. The 'Edit crates' link (route 'crates') and the '+ Add a record' link (route 'album-new') are gated only by v-if="session.signedIn" (line 21). The component has no canEdit check and no crate prop. It takes an optional addToCrateId prop, which only sets the ?crateId query (line 24). A comment at line 6 says 'anyone signed in may make a crate or add a record to one of theirs', so the global display is deliberate. Used by CrateView.vue:89 and LibraryView.vue:149.

Serves /shelf (name 'library') and /crates/:id (name 'crate'); both can show another user's crate. canEditThisCrate = canEditCrate(session.user, crate) (line 76). Line 89 passes add-to-crate-id only when editable, so the toolbar's Add a record button still renders on someone else's crate, just without the crate preselected. The 'Nothing in here yet. Add a record' link at 148-153 is already gated by canEditThisCrate. The crate is picked from the URL or the selection tab (30-32, 111-124). There is no other 'add' control in this file.

The /list view shows all crates. Per-crate 'add' links, drag, move tools and the 'Drag a record here' text are already gated by canEditCrate. The global LibraryToolbar at line 149 has the same ungated Edit crates and Add a record buttons.

Route /crates, reached from the toolbar 'Edit crates' link. Lists only editable crates (line 16). The

New crate

plus CrateSettings :crate=null form (111-117) is always shown to anyone who reaches the page. It is not a view of another user's crate.
'Make your first crate' link, shown only when there are no crates.
Filters the crate picker with canEditCrate. Line 62 rejects the original album's crate if it is not editable. Line 210 links to 'Make a crate.' when none is editable.

/u/:username lists that user's crates as links to the 'crate' route. It has no add or new-crate control; the only session-gated element is at line 124. Reaching another user's crate goes through CrateView.
Routes: /shelf, /list, /crates, /crates/:id, /albums/new. A guard at 121-122 redirects to login with ?next. I did not read the guard's conditions.

api_enforcement.summary: Every write is already enforced server-side, so the fix is UI-only.

files.note: requireUser throws 401. canEditOwner (21-25) allows an admin or the owner, and ownerless crates are admin-only. assertCanEditCrate (28-40) throws 404 for a missing crate and 403 'You can only change crates you own'. assertCanEditAlbum (43-56) applies the same rule through the album's crate. requireAdmin is at 59-63.

Creating a crate (POST /api/crates) needs requireUser and sets ownerId to the creator (92, 101). Update and delete call assertCanEditCrate (114, 122). Reorder (137, 151) refuses a non-admin unless they own every crate on the shelf.

Creating an album checks requireUser plus assertCanEditCrate on fields.crateId (118-120). Updates, moves, deletes and other writes call assertCanEditAlbum, and assertCanEditCrate on the destination crate.
Cover writes call assertCanEditAlbum. The route is apps/api/src/routes/covers.ts:15.

web.note: Most relevant test file. Line 152 'list view offers move tools and add links only on crates the user owns' covers the per-crate controls. Lines 174-176 assert that Edit crates and + Add a record show for any signed-in user, which is the current behaviour a fix would change. Lines 184-189 cover signed-out users. Lines 226-228 check the owner's crate page gets the href /albums/new?crateId=1. Lines 236-238 check that on someone else's crate (/crates/2 as alice) the href is plain /albums/new, so the button is still present. The helper addRecord is at 219. The file sets up fixtures alice, admin, and crates with different owners, including a legacy ownerless one (line 28).

Crate browser tests; ownerId is null in the fixture (line 18). It has a block 'the crate controls on /crates/:id' (288-326) with Flip, Pull, owner link and empty-crate cases. It has no assertion about add or new-crate visibility.
Only register the 'crate' route; not relevant to the add controls.

api.note: Covers ownerId on create (104-117), the owner-or-admin rules, 403 for non-owners, and admin overrides (222-237).
Crate CRUD and validation (line 60 'validates new crates').
Fixture helper that inserts a crate with a given ownerId.

docs: /Users/thomasfuhriman/code/crate-digger/README.md:72 (signed-in users create crates and edit only their own)
notes: The user's wording matches the global toolbar, which has no per-crate gating. The 'New crate' form is a separate page (/crates) reached through 'Edit crates'. It lists only the user's own crates and is not a view of someone else's crate.

The toolbar is also rendered on /list (LibraryView), where there is no single current crate. A fix that hides the toolbar actions on another user's crate would only change /shelf and /crates/:id, because CrateView passes the crate context.
I did not check whether any other component links to 'crates' or 'album-new'. The grep found only LibraryToolbar, LibraryView:233, CrateView:150 and EmptyShelf/AlbumEditorView.
